profiles.standard_full_name: AS9100D:2016 - Quality Management Systems - Requirements for Aviation, Space and Defense Organizations
profiles.vera_knowledge_summary: AS9100D is the aerospace quality standard based on ISO 9001:2015 with additional aerospace-specific requirements. Key additions include configuration management, counterfeit parts prevention, FOD prevention, key characteristics, special requirements, and enhanced risk management focused on product safety and operational safety.
profiles.strategic_intent: Ensure quality management systems in aerospace supply chains consistently produce safe and reliable products. Provides framework for risk-based thinking, configuration control, and supply chain management critical to aviation safety.

typical_implementations.small_organizations: Focus on core QMS processes, manual configuration control, basic supplier evaluation
typical_implementations.medium_organizations: Electronic document control, formal configuration management, supplier performance monitoring
typical_implementations.large_organizations: Integrated QMS systems, enterprise configuration management, comprehensive supplier development programs

typical_gaps: Configuration management not applied consistently across all products
Risk-based thinking not used to drive decisions
Supplier control weakens after initial approval
Key characteristics not identified or controlled

industry_variations.aircraft_manufacturing: Strong focus on design control, configuration management, production approval
industry_variations.component_manufacturing: Emphasis on special processes, first article inspection, supplier control
industry_variations.repair_stations: Focus on maintenance processes, technical data control, personnel qualifications

profiles.vera_knowledge_summary: ISO 9001:2015 is the foundational international standard for quality management systems. It provides a framework for organizations to demonstrate their ability to consistently provide products and services that meet customer and regulatory requirements. Key focus areas include risk-based thinking, process approach, and continual improvement.
profiles.strategic_intent: Provide a framework for quality management that enables organizations to enhance customer satisfaction through effective application of the system, including processes for continual improvement and assurance of conformity to customer and applicable statutory and regulatory requirements.

typical_implementations.small_organizations: Manual processes, simple document control, basic procedures
typical_implementations.medium_organizations: Electronic systems, formal processes, structured improvement
typical_implementations.large_organizations: Integrated management systems, enterprise-wide processes, sophisticated improvement programs

typical_gaps: Risk-based thinking not implemented, just documented
Document control not maintained over time
Corrective actions don't address root causes
Objectives not measurable or not monitored

industry_variations.manufacturing: Strong process controls, product verification, supplier management
industry_variations.services: Service delivery processes, customer interaction management
industry_variations.software: Development lifecycle controls, version management, testing

profiles.standard_full_name: ISO 13485:2016 - Medical devices - Quality management systems - Requirements for regulatory purposes
profiles.vera_knowledge_summary: ISO 13485 is the quality management standard for medical devices. Based on ISO 9001 but tailored for medical device regulatory requirements. Key differences include enhanced design controls, risk management integration (per ISO14971), sterile barrier systems, installation and servicing requirements, and regulatory notification requirements.
profiles.strategic_intent: Ensure medical device organizations have quality management systems that enable them to consistently meet customer and regulatory requirements. Focus on patient safety, risk management, and regulatory compliance.

typical_implementations.device_manufacturers: Comprehensive design controls, risk management files, UDI implementation
typical_implementations.contract_manufacturers: Production controls, supplier management, sterilization validation

typical_gaps: Design controls not comprehensive or not followed
Risk management not integrated throughout lifecycle
Regulatory requirements not identified or tracked

industry_variations.class_i_devices: Basic QMS requirements, less design control emphasis
industry_variations.class_ii_devices: Full design controls, clinical evaluation required
industry_variations.class_iii_devices: Enhanced requirements, comprehensive clinical data, post-market surveillance
